newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-PRESIDENTS CUP SET FOR AUSTRALIA'S MELBOURNE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRESIDENTS CUP SET FOR AUSTRALIA'S MELBOURNE.

text.p: The southern Australian city of Melbourne will host the 1998 Presidents Cup international team golf tournament -- the first time the event would be staged outside the United States since its inauguration in 1994.
Prime Minister John Howard on Monday said the tournament would focus the attention of the sporting world on Australia.
"It is an event that will receive worldwide extensive coverage," Howard said.

The event will be staged at The Royal Melbourne Golf Club in December 1998 and organisers hope U.S. President Bill Clinton, who supported the idea of Australia hosting the Presidents Cup during his visit last year, will attend the event.
The biennial match play event, in which a U.S. team plays against an international squad, has been won by the United States both times it has been played.
The 1998 International team would be led by Australian Peter Thomson who took the interationals to within a point of victory in 1996.
